requirements.title: ACM Problem-Solving Platform
requirements.description: A website designed to help users solve ACM-style programming problems and improve their coding skills.

features.name: Problem Library
features.description: A comprehensive library of ACM-style programming problems categorized by difficulty and topic.

features.name: Code Submission and Evaluation
features.description: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive instant feedback on correctness and performance.

features.name: User Profiles and Progress Tracking
features.description: Enables users to create profiles, track their progress, and view their problem-solving history.

features.name: Leaderboard
features.description: Displays a leaderboard to encourage competition among users based on problem-solving performance.

features.name: Hints and Explanations
features.description: Provides hints and detailed explanations for problems to help users learn and improve.

constraints: The platform must handle a large number of concurrent users.
Code evaluation should be efficient and secure to prevent abuse.
requirements.target_users: Students, competitive programmers, and individuals preparing for coding competitions.
requirements.data_requirements: The platform needs to store user profiles, problem data, submission history, and leaderboard information.

tasks.name: Design Problem Library UI
tasks.description: Create the frontend interface for browsing and searching problems in the library.

tasks.name: Implement Problem Library Backend
tasks.description: Develop the backend logic to store, retrieve, and manage problems in the library.

tasks.name: Set Up Problem Database
tasks.description: Design and implement the database schema for storing problem details.

tasks.name: Develop Code Submission UI
tasks.description: Create the frontend interface for users to submit their code solutions.

tasks.name: Implement Code Evaluation System
tasks.description: Develop the backend logic to evaluate submitted code against test cases.

tasks.name: Design User Profile UI
tasks.description: Create the frontend interface for user profiles and progress tracking.

tasks.name: Implement User Profile Backend
tasks.description: Develop the backend logic to manage user profiles and track progress.

tasks.name: Set Up User Database
tasks.description: Design and implement the database schema for storing user information and progress.

tasks.name: Develop Leaderboard UI
tasks.description: Create the frontend interface for displaying the leaderboard.

tasks.name: Implement Leaderboard Backend
tasks.description: Develop the backend logic to calculate and update leaderboard rankings.

tasks.name: Add Hints and Explanations UI
tasks.description: Create the frontend interface for displaying hints and explanations for problems.

tasks.name: Implement Hints and Explanations Backend
tasks.description: Develop the backend logic to manage and serve hints and explanations for problems.

tasks.name: Test Problem Library Functionality
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure the problem library works as expected.

tasks.name: Test Code Submission and Evaluation
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure code submission and evaluation works correctly.

tasks.name: Test User Profiles and Progress Tracking
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure user profiles and progress tracking are accurate.

tasks.name: Test Leaderboard Functionality
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure the leaderboard updates and displays correctly.

tasks.name: Test Hints and Explanations
tasks.description: Perform testing to ensure hints and explanations are displayed correctly.

tasks.name: Deploy ACM Problem-Solving Platform
tasks.description: Deploy the platform to a production environment.

T1.implementation_approach: Design a user-friendly interface for browsing, filtering, and searching problems using modern UI frameworks like React or Angular.
T1.notes: Ensure responsive design for compatibility across devices.

T2.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to handle problem data retrieval, filtering, and search using a framework like Node.js or Django.
T2.notes: Focus on efficient query handling for large datasets.

T3.implementation_approach: Set up a relational database (e.g., PostgreSQL) to store problem details, tags, and metadata.
T3.notes: Ensure proper indexing for fast query performance.

T4.implementation_approach: Create a submission interface allowing users to upload code and view results using a clean and intuitive design.
T4.notes: Include real-time feedback for submission status.

T5.implementation_approach: Develop a system to evaluate code submissions using containerized environments like Docker for security and scalability.
T5.notes: Implement support for multiple programming languages.

T6.implementation_approach: Design a profile UI displaying user details, progress, and achievements using a visually appealing layout.
T6.notes: Include customization options for user profiles.

T7.implementation_approach: Build backend APIs to manage user data, progress tracking, and achievements using secure authentication mechanisms.
T7.notes: Ensure data privacy and encryption for sensitive information.

T8.implementation_approach: Set up a database to store user information, progress, and activity logs using a scalable schema.
T8.notes: Optimize for frequent read and write operations.

T9.implementation_approach: Develop a leaderboard UI to display rankings based on user performance and activity using dynamic sorting and filtering.
T9.notes: Ensure real-time updates for leaderboard changes.

T10.implementation_approach: Implement backend logic to calculate and update leaderboard rankings based on user submissions and scores.
T10.notes: Optimize for high concurrency during peak usage.

T11.implementation_approach: Design a UI to display hints and explanations for problems in an accessible and organized manner.
T11.notes: Allow users to unlock hints progressively to avoid spoilers.

T12.implementation_approach: Develop backend APIs to manage hints and explanations, including retrieval and access control.
T12.notes: Ensure hints are tied to specific problem IDs for accuracy.

T13.implementation_approach: Test the problem library for functionality, including search, filtering, and data retrieval.
T13.notes: Use automated and manual testing methods.

T14.implementation_approach: Test the code submission and evaluation system for accuracy, security, and performance under load.
T14.notes: Simulate various edge cases and invalid inputs.

T15.implementation_approach: Verify user profile features like progress tracking, achievements, and data updates through comprehensive testing.

T16.implementation_approach: Test leaderboard functionality for real-time updates, sorting, and filtering under different scenarios.
T16.notes: Check for concurrency issues during updates.

T17.implementation_approach: Test hints and explanations for proper display, access control, and relevance to problems.
T17.notes: Ensure hints unlock correctly based on user actions.

T18.implementation_approach: Deploy the platform on a cloud service like AWS or Azure, ensuring scalability and security configurations.
T18.notes: Perform final checks for performance and reliability before launch.

from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy

# Initialize SQLAlchemy instance
db = SQLAlchemy()

from app.database import db

class Problem(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'problems'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    difficulty = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    sample_input = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    sample_output = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.current_timestamp())
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, default=db.func.current_timestamp(), onupdate=db.func.current_timestamp())

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Problem {self.id} - {self.title} (Difficulty: {self.difficulty})>"

from app.database import db
from datetime import datetime

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(50), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(128), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow, onupdate=datetime.utcnow)

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<User {self.username}>"

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'username': self.username,
            'email': self.email,
            'created_at': self.created_at.isoformat(),
            'updated_at': self.updated_at.isoformat()
        }

from app.database import db
from app.models.problem import Problem
from app.models.user import User

class Solution(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'solutions'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    code = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=False)
    language = db.Column(db.String(50), nullable=False)
    result = db.Column(db.String(20), nullable=False)  # e.g., "Accepted", "Wrong Answer"
    submission_time = db.Column(db.DateTime, nullable=False, server_default=db.func.now())

    # Foreign key to associate with a User
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id'), nullable=False)
    user = db.relationship('User', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))

    # Foreign key to associate with a Problem
    problem_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('problems.id'), nullable=False)
    problem = db.relationship('Problem', backref=db.backref('solutions', lazy=True))

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"<Solution id={self.id} user_id={self.user_id} problem_id={self.problem_id} result={self.result}>"

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'code': self.code,
            'language': self.language,
            'result': self.result,
            'submission_time': self.submission_time.isoformat(),
            'user_id': self.user_id,
            'problem_id': self.problem_id,
        }

from flask import Blueprint, request, jsonify, render_template
from app.database import db
from app.models.solution import Solution
from app.models.problem import Problem
from app.models.user import User

solution_bp = Blueprint('solution', __name__)

@solution_bp.route('/solutions', methods=['GET'])
def list_solutions():
    """Handles GET requests to '/solutions'."""
    solutions = Solution.query.all()
    solution_list = [solution.to_dict() for solution in solutions]
    return jsonify(solution_list), 200

@solution_bp.route('/solutions/<int:solution_id>', methods=['GET'])
def view_solution(solution_id):
    """Handles GET requests to '/solutions/<int:solution_id>'."""
    solution = Solution.query.get(solution_id)
    if solution:
        return jsonify(solution.to_dict()), 200
    return jsonify({'error': 'Solution not found'}), 404

@solution_bp.route('/solutions/new', methods=['POST'])
def create_solution():
    """Handles POST requests to '/solutions/new'."""
    data = request.json
    user_id = data.get('user_id')
    problem_id = data.get('problem_id')
    content = data.get('content')

    user = User.query.get(user_id)
    problem = Problem.query.get(problem_id)

    if not user or not problem:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Invalid user or problem'}), 400

    new_solution = Solution(user_id=user_id, problem_id=problem_id, content=content)
    db.session.add(new_solution)
    db.session.commit()
    
    return jsonify(new_solution.to_dict()), 201

@solution_bp.route('/solutions/<int:solution_id>/edit', methods=['PUT'])
def edit_solution(solution_id):
    """Handles PUT requests to '/solutions/<int:solution_id>/edit'."""
    solution = Solution.query.get(solution_id)
    if not solution:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Solution not found'}), 404

    data = request.json
    content = data.get('content', solution.content)
    solution.content = content
    
    db.session.commit()
    return jsonify(solution.to_dict()), 200

@solution_bp.route('/solutions/<int:solution_id>/delete', methods=['DELETE'])
def delete_solution(solution_id):
    """Handles DELETE requests to '/solutions/<int:solution_id>/delete'."""
    solution = Solution.query.get(solution_id)
    if not solution:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Solution not found'}), 404

    db.session.delete(solution)
    db.session.commit()
    return jsonify({'message': 'Solution deleted successfully'}), 200

from app.models.problem import Problem
from app.models.user import User
from app.models.solution import Solution
from app.controllers.problem_controller import problem_bp
from app.controllers.user_controller import user_bp
from app.controllers.solution_controller import solution_bp

# Create a blueprint for assembly-level routes
assembly_bp = Blueprint('assembly', __name__)

# Register the blueprints for other layers
def register_routes(app):
    app.register_blueprint(problem_bp, url_prefix='/problems')
    app.register_blueprint(user_bp, url_prefix='/users')
    app.register_blueprint(solution_bp, url_prefix='/solutions')
    app.register_blueprint(assembly_bp)  # Register this blueprint if needed for future routes

# Example route for assembly layer (can be extended as needed)
@assembly_bp.route('/dashboard')
def dashboard():
    # Example: Display counts of problems, users, and solutions
    problem_count = db.session.query(Problem).count()
    user_count = db.session.query(User).count()
    solution_count = db.session.query(Solution).count()
    return render_template('dashboard.html', problem_count=problem_count, 
                           user_count=user_count, solution_count=solution_count)

from flask import Flask, render_template
from app.database import db
from app.routes import register_routes

def create_app():
    # Initialize the Flask app
    app = Flask(
        __name__,
        template_folder='../templates',
        static_folder='../static',
        static_url_path='/static'
    )

    # Configure the app (add your configurations here)
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI'] = 'sqlite:///acm_platform.db'
    app.config['SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS'] = False

    # Initialize the database
    db.init_app(app)

    # Register blueprints using the register_routes function
    register_routes(app)

    # Define the home route
    @app.route('/')
    def home():
        return render_template('index.html')

    return app

from flask import Flask
from app.database import db
from app import create_app
from app.routes import register_routes

# Create the Flask application instance
app = create_app()

# Register all blueprints
register_routes(app)

# Run the application
if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run(debug=True)

from sqlalchemy.exc import SQLAlchemyError

class DatabaseExceptionHandler:
    @staticmethod
    def handle_exception(exception: SQLAlchemyError) -> dict:
        """
        Handles SQLAlchemy exceptions and returns a structured response.

        Args:
            exception (SQLAlchemyError): The exception raised by SQLAlchemy.

        Returns:
            dict: A structured response containing error details.
        """
        response = {
            "error": "DatabaseError",
            "message": str(exception),
            "details": exception.__class__.__name__
        }
        return response

# ACM Problem-Solving Platform

A website designed to help users solve ACM-style programming problems and improve their coding skills.

## Features

- Problem Library: A comprehensive library of ACM-style programming problems categorized by difficulty and topic.
- Code Submission and Evaluation: Allows users to submit code solutions and receive instant feedback on correctness and performance.
- User Profiles and Progress Tracking: Enables users to create profiles, track their progress, and view their problem-solving history.
- Leaderboard: Displays a leaderboard to encourage competition among users based on problem-solving performance.
- Hints and Explanations: Provides hints and detailed explanations for problems to help users learn and improve.

## Setup

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```

## Usage

Open http://localhost:5000 in your browser.
